answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce a ferrous barrier against identity proliferation, as slashing penalties within a subgame-perfect punishment matrix ensure the expected utility of Sybil multiplication remains strictly negative. By integrating a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, the protocol forces any gale of spoofed validator nodes to exhaust collateral reserves that exceed the marginal block rewards. We thread these security primitives into a robust Nash equilibrium, proving that deviations by adversarial agents result in immediate capital forfeiture.
